rubric.item: SPEC-02 correctness (incl. section 7 never-unblocked retries, J-1-01)

findings.issue: The `void settled.then(() => { if (blockedOpen === settled) blockedOpen = null; })` reset is not needed for behaviour: once the blocked request settles, awaiting the already-resolved `blockedOpen` wins the race immediately, and a later blocked open overwrites it. It adds a second piece of state bookkeeping that a reader has to reason about.
findings.evidence: Mutation in a scratch worktree: deleting the reset leaves all 5 tests in tests/storage/upgrade-blocked.test.ts passing; tracing the code, the only effect is one extra microtask per call after a blocked open has settled.
findings.fix: Either drop the reset and set `blockedOpen = settled` directly in the onBlocked callback, or keep it and accept it as tidy-up; no behaviour change either way.

findings.issue: `db === opening` in the catch handler is still always true: `db` is only assigned when it is null, and only this handler sets it back to null.
findings.evidence: database() assigns db only inside `if (db === null)`; the sole reset is this catch.
findings.fix: Drop `&& db === opening`, or keep it as a cheap guard.

findings.issue: The openHandStore docblock still has a line of about 170 characters, far past the file's ~120-column comment width (Prettier does not rewrap comments).
findings.evidence: ` * still pending, calls reject with UpgradeBlockedError after a short wait. Records are validated by parseHandRecord / parseSessionRecord / ...`
findings.fix: Rewrap the docblock to the surrounding width.

summary: J-1-01 is fixed. While a blocked open request is still pending, database() waits at most BLOCKED_GRACE_MS (100 ms) for it to settle and otherwise throws UpgradeBlockedError instead of starting a new open that would queue behind it. opened() hands the caller a promise that resolves on the late success (after closing that connection) or on the late error, so the next call after the blocker closes retries and succeeds (SPEC-03). Tests: the new 'a call made while the upgrade is still blocked rejects promptly' test fails on the r1 code (it times out at 5000 ms, checked by running the test against hand-store.ts from 7df99f4 in a scratch worktree, which was then removed). Removing the wait (throw at once while blocked) fails 2 tests, because the 100 ms grace is what lets SPEC-03's call right after blocker.close() succeed. The r1 MINOR is addressed: removing `db.close()` from the late-success branch makes 'a blocked open that later succeeds closes its connection' fail. Setting the grace to 0 ms still passes, so the 100 ms value itself is not pinned. That is acceptable because the spec gives no number. All 7 storage tests pass locally. The UI/e2e parts did not change since r1, when they passed. No BLOCKER or MAJOR findings. There is one MINOR (an unneeded blockedOpen reset) and two NITs carried over from r1.
